title: PRG32 and PRG32-QT: Setting Up Your Workshop

quiz.q: In a new terminal, python3 -m prg32 doctor says: idf.py missing. What is the most likely cause?
opts: ESP-IDF is not active in this terminal
quiz.why: Activation lasts as long as the terminal: run export.sh, or open the ESP-IDF PowerShell.

quiz.q: Which host lets you run and debug a cartridge without installing a compiler?
quiz.why: PRG32-QT interprets the cartridge and has a built-in debugger; a compiler is needed only to build cartridges.

quiz.q: Why does the same pong.prg32 run on the board, on QEMU and on PRG32-QT?
opts: it is recompiled at each start
it calls the runtime through the same table of functions on every host
quiz.why: A portable cartridge depends only on the ABI, the table of functions of the runtime, which every host provides.

quiz.q: What does an assembler do?
opts: it runs the program on the processor
it translates assembly source code into machine code
it sends the cartridge to a host
quiz.why: Assembly is text for people; the processor reads numbers. The assembler translates the first into the second; the runtime of a host then runs the result.

title: First Contact: RISC-V Assembly on PRG32

quiz.q: After la t0, counter and lw t1, 0(t0), what does t0 hold?
opts: Zero, because la clears the register
quiz.why: la loads the address of the label; lw then reads the value stored at that address into t1.

quiz.q: A function that calls prg32_gfx_clear must save one register before the call. Which one?
opts: a0, because it carries the argument
quiz.why: call writes the return address in ra. The callee's own calls would overwrite it, so a non-leaf function saves ra on the stack and restores it before ret.

quiz.q: t1 holds 300. What does andi a2, t1, 255 leave in a2?
quiz.why: 300 = 256 + 44 = 1 0010 1100 in binary. AND with 1111 1111 keeps the low eight bits: 0010 1100 = 44.

quiz.q: What number is 0x1F?
quiz.why: 0x marks a hexadecimal number. 1 means one sixteen and F means fifteen units: 16 + 15 = 31, which is 1 1111 in binary.

quiz.q: Which idea is the heart of the von Neumann architecture?
opts: The processor has exactly four registers
Program and data are stored in the same memory
Every instruction takes one clock cycle
quiz.why: The stored-program concept: instructions are data in memory, fetched and executed one after another.

quiz.q: What makes RISC-V different from x86 and ARM?
opts: It is the fastest instruction set
It was the first RISC architecture
Its instruction set is an open standard, free to implement
quiz.why: RISC-V is an open standard instruction set architecture; anyone may design and sell a RISC-V processor without an architecture licence. It was not the first RISC (Berkeley RISC, MIPS, ARM came earlier).

quiz.q: Who is regarded as the first programmer in history?
quiz.why: Ada Lovelace, for her 1843 notes on the Analytical Engine.

quiz.q: How many different values can one byte represent?
quiz.why: A byte is 8 bits: 2^8 = 256 patterns, for example the naturals from 0 to 255.

quiz.q: The PRG32 colour 0xF81F is:
quiz.why: 0xF81F = 11111 000000 11111: red and blue at maximum, green at zero: magenta.

quiz.q: How many bytes does .asciz "CIAO" occupy in memory?
quiz.why: Four characters plus the terminating zero byte.

quiz.q: On RISC-V, .word 0x0000ABCD is stored at address A. Which byte is at address A?
quiz.why: RISC-V is little-endian: the least significant byte, 0xCD, goes at the lowest address.

quiz.q: Which number does the 8-bit pattern 1111 1100 represent in two's complement?
quiz.why: Complement and add one: 0000 0011 + 1 = 0000 0100 = 4, so the pattern is -4. (252 is its unsigned reading.)

quiz.q: On 8 bits, which addition produces a signed overflow?
quiz.why: The range is [-128, 127]. 100 + 27 = 127 fits; 100 + 28 = 128 does not: two positives give a negative pattern (1000 0000 = -128).

quiz.q: t0 holds 0xFFFFFFFF and t1 holds 1. After slt t2, t0, t1 and sltu t3, t0, t1:
quiz.why: Signed: -1 < 1 is true, so t2 = 1. Unsigned: 4,294,967,295 < 1 is false, so t3 = 0.

quiz.q: How is 0.625 written in binary?
Which signed encoding keeps the bit patterns in the same order as the numbers?
quiz.why: In excess-k, X = x + k: a larger number always has a larger pattern. This is why it encodes floating-point exponents, which must be compared quickly.

quiz.q: In Q24.8 fixed point, which real number does the word 0x00000180 represent?
Which real number is the IEEE 754 single-precision pattern 0x40400000?
In IEEE 754, an exponent field of all ones with a fraction of all zeros means:
quiz.why: All ones in the exponent: infinity if the fraction is zero, NaN otherwise.

title: Verm1, Part 1: A Head That Crosses the World

quiz.q: With SPEED_Q8 = 64, how many frames pass between two steps of the head?
quiz.why: 64/256 = 1/4 of a cell per frame: a whole cell every 4 frames.

quiz.q: Which pixel is the top-left corner of the cell in column 10, row 3?
Why does verm1_draw save ra and verm1_update does not?
opts: draw calls other functions, which overwrite ra
ra is saved automatically in update
quiz.why: A call writes the return address in ra. A function that makes calls must keep its own ra safe on the stack; a leaf function need not.

quiz.q: For which inputs is x NAND y equal to 0?
quiz.why: NAND is the complement of AND: it is 0 only when both inputs are 1.

quiz.q: By De Morgan, (a . b')' is equal to:
quiz.why: (a . b')' = a' + (b')' = a' + b, using involution on the second term.

quiz.q: t0 = 0x0000005A. What is in t1 after andi t1, t0, 0x0F?
quiz.why: 0x5A = 0101 1010; AND with 0000 1111 keeps the low nibble: 1010 = 0xA.

quiz.q: Which instruction turns bit 5 of t0 to 1 and leaves every other bit unchanged?
quiz.why: OR with a mask: x + 1 = 1 on bit 5, x + 0 = x elsewhere. xori would toggle it; addi would carry into bit 6 if the bit was already 1.

quiz.q: How many distinct Boolean functions of three variables are there?
Which minterm of three variables A, B, C corresponds to row 5 of the truth table?
quiz.why: Row 5 is 101: A = 1, B = 0, C = 1, so the minterm is A B' C.

quiz.q: In a Karnaugh map, a rectangular group of four adjacent 1s eliminates:
quiz.why: A group of 2^k cells eliminates k variables: four cells, two variables.

quiz.q: In a full adder, the carry out is 1 when:
opts: an odd number of inputs is 1
quiz.why: Cout is the majority function: AB + Cin(A xor B) = AB + ACin + BCin. An odd number of 1s describes the sum bit S instead.

title: Introduction to Electronics and Digital Electronics

quiz.q: An LED drops 2 V and must carry 5 mA from a 3.3 V pin. Which resistor is needed?
In a CMOS inverter with the input at 0:
opts: the pMOS conducts and the output is 1
the nMOS conducts and the output is 0
neither conducts and the output floats
quiz.why: A low gate closes the pMOS, which joins the output to the supply; the nMOS is open.

quiz.q: How many transistors does a two-input AND need in static CMOS?
quiz.why: A NAND (4) followed by an inverter (2).

quiz.q: Why does the button input of the kit need a pull-up resistor?
opts: To limit the current of the LED
To make the pin read a defined 1 when the button is released
To protect the chip from 5 V
quiz.why: Without it the released pin would float; the pull-up ties it to 3.3 V, and the pressed switch overrides it to ground.

quiz.q: How many bits does a fixed-length binary code need for the 26 letters of the alphabet?
quiz.why: ceil(log2 26) = 5, since 2^4 = 16 < 26 <= 32 = 2^5. Six words remain unassigned: the code is incomplete.

quiz.q: A decoder has 3 input lines and no enable. How many outputs does it have, and how many are 1 at any time?
quiz.why: 2^3 = 8 outputs, and exactly one is asserted: the decoded (one-hot) representation of the input word.

quiz.q: A multiplexer with 8 data inputs needs how many selection lines?
quiz.why: n selection lines choose among 2^n inputs: 3 lines for 8 inputs.

quiz.q: A word with one even-parity bit is received with two bits altered. The parity check:
opts: detects the error and corrects it
detects the error but cannot correct it
signals an error only if both bits were 1
quiz.why: Two alterations leave the parity unchanged. A single parity bit detects only an odd number of errors.

title: Verm1, Part 2: Steering, Food and a Score

quiz.q: The player holds DOWN and RIGHT together: prg32_input_read returns
quiz.why: 0x08 OR 0x02 = 0x0a: one bit per button.

quiz.q: The worm goes UP (3). Which wish is refused?
quiz.why: 3 XOR 1 = 2: DOWN is the opposite of UP.

quiz.q: Why slli t1, t1, 2 before adding to the address of dx?
opts: each entry of the table is 4 bytes
quiz.why: The entries are words: entry k is at offset 4k.

quiz.q: xor t1, t1, t4 gives zero exactly when
quiz.why: XOR is 1 where bits differ: no difference, all zeros.

quiz.q: In a Moore machine the output depends on:
opts: the present state and the present input
the next state and the input
quiz.why: Moore: w maps S to U. In a Mealy machine the output depends on the state and on the input.

quiz.q: An SR latch built with NOR gates has Q = 1. S and R are both 0. What happens?
quiz.why: S = R = 0 is the hold condition: the feedback keeps the stored value.

quiz.q: What distinguishes a D flip-flop from a D latch?
opts: The flip-flop changes only on a clock edge
The flip-flop does not need a clock
quiz.why: The latch is transparent for the whole active level of the clock; the flip-flop samples D only on the edge.

quiz.q: How many flip-flops are needed for a finite-state machine with 10 states?
quiz.why: ceil(log2 10) = 4 state variables, with the minimum-length binary code of Lecture 11. Ten would be needed with a one-hot code.

quiz.q: Why does a common bus need three-state buffers?
opts: So that only the enabled source drives the lines
To store the datum on the bus
To convert serial data to parallel
quiz.why: Several sources share the same lines; all but one must be electrically disconnected (high impedance), otherwise two outputs would fight over the wire.

quiz.q: How many clock pulses does a serial transfer of a 32-bit word need?
quiz.why: One bit per pulse: n pulses for n bits. A parallel transfer needs one pulse and n wires.

quiz.q: A memory has 10 address lines and 8 data lines. How many bits does it store?
quiz.why: 2^10 = 1,024 words of 8 bits: 8,192 bits, that is 1 KiB.

quiz.q: A memory has 16 address lines and is byte-addressable. How large is it?
quiz.why: 2^16 = 65,536 locations of one byte: 64 KiB, the address space of a Commodore 64.

quiz.q: On RISC-V, value: .word 0xCAFE0001 is at address A. What does lbu t0, 0(t0) read if t0 = A?
quiz.why: Little-endian: the least significant byte, 0x01, is at the lowest address.

quiz.q: Why must DRAM be refreshed?
opts: Because its capacitors lose their charge
Because it is not random access
Because the clock is too fast
quiz.why: Each bit is a charge in a capacitor that leaks away; a circuit inside the memory rewrites every cell periodically.

quiz.q: How does a RISC-V program write to an output device?
opts: With sw to the address of a device register
It cannot: only the firmware can
quiz.why: RISC-V has no I/O instructions: devices are memory-mapped and reached with ordinary loads and stores.

quiz.q: Which memory can be erased electrically, in blocks, without removing it from the board?
quiz.why: Flash is the block-erasable evolution of EEPROM. EPROM needs ultraviolet light; ROM and PROM cannot be erased.

quiz.q: What happens on a cache miss?
opts: The program stops with an error
The datum is fetched from main memory and copied into the cache, with its neighbours
quiz.why: The access is simply slower: the block containing the address is loaded into the cache, betting that nearby addresses will be needed soon.

quiz.q: Which component of the access time of a hard disk depends on the rotation speed?
quiz.why: Latency is the wait for the sector to arrive under the head; seek time depends on the movement of the arm.

quiz.q: On an optical disk, a 1 is encoded as:
opts: a transition between pit and land
quiz.why: A change of reflectivity, in either direction, is a 1; no change is a 0.

title: Verm1, Part 3: A Body, Rules and States

quiz.q: head_i = 1 and length = 4. Which entries of the ring hold the worm?
quiz.why: From the tail, head_i - length + 1 = -2, that is 254 after AND 255, up to the head: 254, 255, 0, 1.

quiz.q: Which byte of grid describes the cell in column 7 of row 3?
The player holds A down for two seconds on the title screen. What happens?
opts: the game starts and ends at once
the states cycle at every frame
quiz.why: Only the frame in which A goes down gives s1 = 0x10: one edge, one transition.

quiz.q: Why is the tail's byte cleared before the head's byte is tested?
opts: so that the head can enter the cell the tail leaves
because sb is faster than lbu
quiz.why: In the same step the tail moves away: that cell is free for the head.

quiz.q: Which register of the general model has no counterpart in RISC-V?
opts: the status register with the flags
quiz.why: RISC-V has no condition codes: branches compare registers directly.

quiz.q: In RISC-V, which instructions can read or write the main memory?
quiz.why: It is a load-store architecture: lw, lh, lb, sw, sh, sb and their unsigned forms.

quiz.q: After addi sp, sp, -4 and sw t0, 0(sp), what has happened?
opts: t0 was popped from the stack
t0 was pushed on the stack
quiz.why: The pointer moves down by one word and the value is stored on the new top: a push.

quiz.q: In an accumulator machine, the instruction ADD y means:
quiz.why: The accumulator is the implicit operand and the destination.

quiz.q: In which bits of a RISC-V instruction is the opcode?
quiz.why: Bits 6 to 0, in every format: the processor always knows where to look first.

quiz.q: During the fetch of an RV32 instruction that is not compressed, the PC is increased by:
quiz.why: Addresses count bytes and an instruction is four bytes long.

quiz.q: Which register holds the address at which an interrupted RISC-V program will resume?
quiz.why: mepc, written by the hardware at the trap and used by mret. mtvec holds the address of the handler.

quiz.q: Which of these is an exception rather than an interrupt, in RISC-V terms?
opts: a packet arrives from the network
quiz.why: It is caused by the instruction being executed, synchronously; the others come from outside, at any moment.

quiz.q: How much memory does a frame of 640 x 480 pixels need in True Color (24 bits)?
quiz.why: 307,200 pixels x 3 bytes = 921,600 bytes.

quiz.q: A 16-bit bus works at 50 MHz, one transfer per cycle. What is its transfer rate?
quiz.why: 2 bytes x 50 million transfers per second = 100 MB/s.

quiz.q: In an 8-bit indexed frame buffer, the byte of a pixel contains:
opts: the position of its colour in a palette
quiz.why: The byte is an index; the actual colour is looked up in a table of 256 entries, the palette.

quiz.q: What is GPGPU?
opts: Using graphics processors for non-graphical computation
quiz.why: General-purpose computing on graphics processing units.

title: Input and Output

quiz.q: What does the encoder of a keyboard controller do?
opts: It lights the key that was pressed
It turns a row and column combination into a key code
It sends the code to the monitor
It counts how long a key is held
quiz.why: From a decoded position in the key matrix to a compact n-bit code, as the encoder of Lecture 11.

quiz.q: In a colour LCD, a pixel is made of:
opts: three cells with red, green and blue filters
a phosphor dot hit by electrons
quiz.why: Three sub-pixels, each a liquid crystal cell behind a colour filter; a TFT in each stores its state.

quiz.q: Why does a passive-matrix LCD show trails behind moving objects?
opts: Its pixels are driven one at a time and must hold their state in between
quiz.why: Persistence: without a transistor per pixel, the cells respond slowly and keep their state badly while the others are scanned.

quiz.q: A PRG32 game reads the joystick once per frame. This technique is called:
quiz.why: The program asks the device periodically. With interrupts the device would call the program.

gloss: stampante ad aghi / a getto d'inchiostro

quiz.q: to_decimal receives a0 = 205. Which bytes does it store, from offset 0 to 2?
quiz.why: The characters '2', '0', '5': 0x32, 0x30, 0x35. The units are stored at offset 2.

quiz.q: At which score does the worm take one step every 4 frames?
quiz.why: One step every 4 frames is 64/256: 32 + 4 x score = 64, so score = 8.

quiz.q: dirty is 0 when verm1_draw is called. How many machine instructions does it execute?
quiz.why: la is two instructions, auipc and addi; then lw, beqz and ret.

quiz.q: Why can to_decimal do without a stack frame?
opts: it calls no function and uses only a and t registers
quiz.why: A leaf function that touches only caller-saved registers has nothing to save.

quiz.q: You published version 1.0.0 and found a bug. What do you do?
opts: ask for the old file to be edited
quiz.why: A published version is treated as permanent: a correction is a new version with the same id.

quiz.q: Why does metadata.json not contain the architectures entry?
opts: the metadata goes inside one cartridge, which has one architecture
quiz.why: The list of files belongs to the bundle; a single cartridge states its own architecture, given on the command line.

quiz.q: Where should the Store token be kept?
opts: in an environment variable of your shell
in the README of the repository
quiz.why: A token is a credential: it never goes into a file that is shared or versioned.

title: Beyond One Core: Superscalar RISC-V, HPC, GPUs and FPGAs

quiz.q: A program is 80% parallel. What is the largest speed-up that any number of processors can give?
quiz.why: With n unlimited, S = 1 / (1 - p) = 1 / 0.2 = 5.

quiz.q: What does register renaming remove?
opts: false dependences between uses of the same register name
quiz.why: Two unrelated values that share a name get different physical registers and can be computed at the same time.

quiz.q: With 256-bit vector registers, how many turns does the vector loop need for the 960 bytes?
quiz.why: 256 bits are 32 bytes per turn: 960 / 32 = 30. The code does not change.

quiz.q: A two-input look-up table stores, for inputs 00, 01, 10, 11, the bits 0, 1, 1, 1. Which gate is it?
quiz.why: The output is 1 whenever at least one input is 1: OR.
